rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctuary’s protection during Quraysh’s two journeys enabled their food supply after earlier hunger.
rows.anchor: لما آمنهم بالحرم حتى لا يتعرض لهم في رحلتيهم كان ذلك سبب إطعامهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Because Yemen and Syria journeys for provisions were arduous, God moved Ethiopians to ship food to Mecca; Meccans traded camels and wine at Jeddah, ending the need for both journeys.
rows.anchor: شق عليهم الذهاب إلى اليمن والشام في الشتاء والصيف لطلب الرزق

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: After Quraysh rejected Muhammad, his prayer for years like Joseph’s famine brought drought; their plea led him to pray, and fertility returned to Mecca.
rows.anchor: لما كذبوا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fed them before they worshipped, so they should trust that He will feed them if they worship; this answers anxiety that worship leaves no time to earn food or defend themselves.
rows.anchor: الذي أطعمهم من جوع ، قبل أن يعبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even after humans mistreat God by disobeying Him, He still feeds them, which should make them ashamed and grateful.
rows.anchor: بعد أن أعطى العبد أصول النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning food reminds people that even an animal obeys whoever feeds it; humans should not be worse.
rows.anchor: لأن البهيمة تطيع من يعلفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food is a divine favor because the celestial spheres, four elements, and varied bodily organs are all needed to produce and use it.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من العناصر الأربعة حتى يتم ذلك الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning food is guidance toward what is best, not an attempt to boast of a favor: eating should strengthen the body for worship, not appetite against it.
rows.anchor: ليس الغرض منه المنة ، بل الإرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from hunger stresses hunger’s severity; the verse about rain after despair illustrates relief after desperate need.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن أمر الجوع شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recall of their former painful hunger teaches them to value their present blessing.
rows.anchor: تذكيرهم الحالة الأولى الرديئة المؤلمة وهي الجوع حتى يعرفوا قدر النعمة الحاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best food is what removes hunger; the wording avoids praising fullness, which produces gluttony.
rows.anchor: خير الطعام ما سد الجوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of security is that Quraysh traveled and stayed safely from raids, unlike other people; the sanctuary is likewise described as secure.
rows.anchor: كانوا يسافرون آمنين لا يتعرض لهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God protected Mecca’s people from the army of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: أنه آمنهم من زحمة أصحاب الفيل

rows.speaker: الضحاك والربيع
rows.claim: They interpret the security as protection from fear of leprosy in their town.
rows.anchor: وآمنهم من خوف الجزام ، فلا يصيبهم ببلدتهم الجذام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that they were relieved of fear that the caliphate would belong to someone else.
rows.anchor: آمنهم من خوف أن تكون الخلافة في غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God secured them through Islam: before Muhammad’s mission they doubted their religion without knowing the true one, then revelation taught them scripture and wisdom and reversed who was called learned or ignorant.
rows.anchor: فقد كانوا في الكفر يتفكرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding bodily hunger merits gratitude; feeding spiritual hunger with revelation and removing fear of misguidance through guidance merits it even more.
rows.anchor: ثم إطعام الطعام الذي يكون غذاء الجسد يوجب الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using مِن rather than عن means God feeds them when they hunger and secures them when they fear; عن would imply they first endured hunger or fear for a time before it was removed.
rows.anchor: لأن معنى عن أنه جعل الجوع بعيدا عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording may magnify hunger and fear: famine was so severe they ate carrion and charred bones, while fear came from the army of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: حتى أكلوا الجيف والعظام المحرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, indefiniteness may belittle even slight hunger and fear: God’s generosity would not leave them in either, so He would not neglect them if they worshipped.
rows.anchor: لما لم يجوز لغاية كرمه إبقاءهم في ذلك الجوع القليل والخوف القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the repeated indefinite terms recall their former varieties of hunger and fear, making them grateful for relief and patient through trials so they earn both rewards.
rows.anchor: ليكون الجوع الثاني ، والخوف الثاني مذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abraham prayed for provision and security, God extended worldly provision to believers and unbelievers, unlike religious security, which is restricted to the pious; thus the Meccans’ food and safety were direct divine favors.
rows.anchor: وأما نعمة الدنيا فهي تصل إلى البر والفاجر والصالح والطالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham first learned that God’s covenant would not reach wrongdoers, then requested security and provision for believers; God answered that even disbelievers would receive temporary provision.
rows.anchor: فنادى إبراهيم بهذا الأدب ، فحين قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter Al-Ma'un is Meccan and consists of seven verses.
rows.anchor: سبع آيات مكية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read أريت, deleting the hamza; al-Zajjaj considers it nonpreferred, since Arabs do not use ريت for the past, though the initial interrogative may ease deletion; a cited line supplies a parallel.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعضهم أريت بحذف الهمزة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads أرأيتك with an added second-person suffix, as in another Quranic expression.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود أرأيتك بزيادة حرف الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arayta asks whether the listener knows who denies the recompense; if not, the answer is the one who pushes away the orphan.
rows.anchor: معناه هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though phrased as a question, the expression intensifies amazement, like asking what someone has done and why he exposed himself to danger.
rows.anchor: اللفظ وإن كان في صورة الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to the Prophet, or to every rational person: why knowingly incur eternal punishment after clear proofs, or trade the lasting great for fleeting worldly gain?
rows.anchor: إنه خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was revealed about Abu Sufyan, who slaughtered two camels weekly but struck an orphan who asked him for meat.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي سفيان كان ينحر جزورين في كل أسبوع

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says it was revealed about al-Asi ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who combined denial of Judgment with ugly deeds.
rows.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira as the person concerned.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that the verse concerned Abu Jahl, a ward’s guardian who rejected the naked orphan’s request for his own property; Muhammad accompanied him to Abu Jahl, who relented out of fear of spears he imagined beside the Prophet.
rows.anchor: حكى الماوردي أنها نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about a hypocrite who combined stinginess and ostentation.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في منافق جمع بين البخل والمراءاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is general to every denier of Judgment: belief in resurrection drives obedience and restraint, while denial removes that restraint and underlies sins and disbelief.
rows.anchor: أنه عام لكل من كان مكذبا بيوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is denial of religion or Islam, including denial of God, prophethood, resurrection, or any revealed law.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد من يكذب بنفس الدين والإسلام إما لأنه كان منكرا للصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although everyone follows some creed, unqualified din in Islamic usage means Islam; other creeds are named only with a qualifier such as the religion of Christians or Jews.
rows.anchor: الدين المطلق في اصطلاح أهل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that false doctrines are not truly religion, which means submission to God; they amount instead to submission to passion or conjecture.
rows.anchor: أن الدين هو الخضوع لله وهذه المذاهب إنما هي خضوع للشهوة أو للشبهة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators interpret din as accounting and recompense; Razi prefers this because someone who affirms resurrection may reject Islam yet still do good, whereas reckless wrongdoing points to denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: وحمله على هذا الوجه أولى لأن من ينكر الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier is characterized by an active offense against the orphan and an omission of urging food for the poor; the causal fa says disbelief produces orphan abuse.
rows.anchor: ذكر في تعريف من يكذب الدين وصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two acts are examples, not an exhaustive list of the denier’s vices; each points to other bad acts and violates both revelation and human decency.
rows.anchor: كأنه تعالى ذكر في كل واحد من القسمين مثالا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadu means pushing the orphan away with violence and harshness, as in the image of people being driven into Hell.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أنه يدفعه بعنف وجفوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pushing the orphan includes unjustly withholding his right and property, refusing even nonobligatory consolation, and scolding, beating, or humiliating him.
rows.anchor: عن حقه وماله بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading without shadda can mean abandoning the orphan or inviting everyone else while leaving him out; a Prophetic report praises a table that includes an orphan.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يدع أي يتركه ، ولا يدعوه بدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with final long waw can mean inviting the orphan ostentatiously but not feeding him, instead exploiting or coercing him.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يدعو اليتيم أي يدعوه رياء ثم لا يطعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled consonant in يَدُعّ signals habitual conduct, so the threat does not cover an isolated act followed by repentance; believers’ lapses are fleeting, unlike deniers’ persistence.
rows.anchor: يدع بالتشديد معناه أنه يعتاد ذلك فلا يتناول الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not urging may mean failing to urge oneself or others; calling the food the poor person’s suggests it is his due and exposes the denier’s extreme stinginess and hard heart.
rows.anchor: لا يحض نفسه على طعام المسكين وإضافة الطعام إلى المسكين تدل على أن ذلك الطعام حق المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he does not urge others because he expects no reward; denial of resurrection leads to harming the weak and withholding kindness.
rows.anchor: لا يحض غيره على إطعام ذلك المسكين بسبب أنه لا يتقد في ذلك الفعل ثوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may sometimes fail to urge because someone else acts, he is ignored, or he expects harm; in this verse the cause is specified as denial of Judgment.
rows.anchor: لأنه غيره ينوب منابه أو لأنه لا يقبل قوله أو لمفسدة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says he does not urge feeding rather than that he himself does not feed: one who withholds an orphan’s property would hardly feed a poor person from his own, showing baseness even with others’ wealth.
rows.anchor: إذا منع اليتيم حقه فكيف يطعم المسكين من مال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are praised for urging one another to compassion, truth, and patience, in contrast to withholding aid.
rows.anchor: وتواصوا بالمرحمة * وتواصوا بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One link is that mistreating the orphan and withholding help show hypocrisy, while prayer without humility is an even clearer sign because it concerns service to the Creator.
rows.anchor: معاملة مع المخلوق ، أما الصلاة فإنها خدمة للخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another link answers the objection that prayer restrains indecency: this prayer cannot restrain evil when it consists of ostentation and inattention.
rows.anchor: الصلاة كيف تنهاه عن هذا الفعل المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third link says orphan abuse neglects compassion for God’s creatures, and heedlessness in prayer neglects reverence for God; failing in both completes wretchedness.
rows.anchor: وسهوه في الصلاة تقصير فيما يرجع إلى التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is used for grave crimes, as in warnings against fraud, scribal wrongdoing, and slander.
rows.anchor: إن هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل عند الجريمة الشديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says each person in Hell wails according to his offense, including love of status, tribal zeal, or prayer; the listener should say, Woe to me unless God forgives me.
rows.anchor: كل أحد ينوح في النار بحسب جريمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat covers three sins: heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small aid; since these do not alone make a Muslim hypocrite, commentators explain why the warning is so severe.
rows.anchor: التهديد العظيم بفعل ثلاثة أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred answer limits the description to hypocritical worshippers: their extra punishment for forbidden acts and omitted duties supports al-Shafi‘i’s view that unbelievers are addressed by the subsidiary laws.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب هو العتمد

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: If the verse said inattentive in their prayer, believers would be threatened; inattentent from their prayer means someone who forgets prayer and is wholly disengaged from it.
rows.anchor: ما رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects interpreting heedlessness from prayer simply as abandoning it: the text still calls them worshippers, and abandonment alone is neither hypocrisy nor unbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف لأن السهو عن الصلاة لا يجوز أن يكون مفسرا بترك الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply is that they count as Muslims outwardly but forget prayer in reality, as hypocrites do; total forgetfulness of God’s remembrance throughout prayer marks a hypocrite, while a believer may be inattentive during some parts.
rows.anchor: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلواة قاموا كسالى

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret heedlessness as failure to maintain prayer times and conditions, not caring whether one prays.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many scholars say the Prophet did not forget in prayer; God instead allowed him to perform a forgetful person’s action so the law would be demonstrated more clearly by practice.
rows.anchor: فقال كثير من العلماء : إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما سها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If prophetic or Companion forgetfulness occurred, it was repaired by prostration of forgetfulness, sunnah, or voluntary prayer; inner distraction is another category, while leaving prayer past its time without making it up is hypocritical mockery and worse than simply leaving it.
rows.anchor: سهو الرسول والصحابة وذلك منجبر تارة بسجود السهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hypocrite displays faith while concealing unbelief; a show-off displays extra humility absent from the heart to seem devout, or differs from a hypocrite because his public prayer is better than his private prayer.
rows.anchor: أن المنافق هو المظهر للإيمان المبطن للكفر ، والمرائي المظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligatory prayers and alms should be public as Islamic emblems to prevent suspicion; voluntary worship is usually concealed unless shown to encourage imitation.
rows.anchor: يجب إظهار الفرائض من الصلاة والزكاة لأنها شعائر الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone saw a man prolonging prostration of thanks in a mosque and remarked that it would be admirable if done at home.
rows.anchor: في المسجد رجلا يسجد للشكر وأطالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should neither abandon voluntary worship from embarrassment nor perform it for show; ostentation is difficult to avoid.
rows.anchor: لا يترك النوافل حياء ولا يأتى بها رياء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet compares ostentation’s subtlety to a black ant moving in a dark night over a black stone.
rows.anchor: الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة الظلماء على المسح الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riya is a reciprocal form of showing: the ostentatious person displays deeds, while observers return praise and admiration.
rows.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإرادة لأن المرائي يرى الناس عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness from prayer indicates both praying outside its time and being distracted within it; with ostentation added, prayer must be free from all three conditions.
rows.anchor: إخراجها عن الوقت ، وكون الإنسان غافلا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar answers four traits in Al-Ma‘un: generosity answers stinginess, maintaining prayer answers neglect, worship for God answers ostentation, and sacrificial meat given away answers withholding aid.
rows.anchor: ذكر في هذه السورة في مقابلة تلك الصفات الأربع صفات أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hostile hypocrite will die without a lasting trace, while Muhammad retains good remembrance in this world and abundant reward in the next.
rows.anchor: المنافق الذي يأتي بتلك الأفعال القبيحة المذكورة في تلك السورة سيموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual path has three ranks: absorption in divine light, bodily obedience, and restraining the self from immediate sensual pleasure; the gifts, prayer, and sacrifice correspond to them, while the enemy is the transient desire and lasting goods are spiritual knowledge and happiness.
rows.anchor: أن يكونوا مستغرقين بقلوبهم وأرواحهم في نور جلال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar completes the earlier chapters and supplies the foundation for what follows; Al-Duha praises Muhammad’s prophethood and three worldly favors: refuge as an orphan, guidance, and enrichment.
rows.anchor: في مدح محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام وتفصيل أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Duha names three prophetic assurances: God did not abandon or dislike him, the Hereafter is better, and God will give until he is pleased.
rows.anchor: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Inshirah honors Muhammad through an expanded breast, removal of his burden, and elevation of his name.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : { ورفعنا لك ذكرك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tin honors him by swearing by his land, promising his community rescue from Hell and reward without end.
rows.anchor: أنه أخبر عن خلاص أمته عن النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Iqra honors him through the command to read with God’s name, victory over his opponent, and the special nearness of prostration.
rows.anchor: أنه خصه بالقربة التامة وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qadr’s three excellences are being better than a thousand months, the descent of angels and the Spirit, and peace until dawn.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : نزول : { الملائكة والروح فيها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayyina honors Muhammad’s community as the best creation, promises gardens as their recompense, and states God’s approval of them.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : { ءان * جزاؤهم عند ربهم جنات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zalzala honors the community because earth will testify to their obedience, their deeds will be shown to them with joy, and even an atom of good earns reward; knowledge of God is the greatest good.
rows.anchor: الأرض تشهد يوم القيامة لأمته بالطاعة والعبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Adiyat honors the community by swearing to the qualities of its raiding horses.
rows.anchor: بأن أقسم بخيل الغزاة من أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qari‘a honors his community through heavy scales, a contented life, and seeing their enemies in a blazing fire.
rows.anchor: ثم شرف أمته في سورة القارعة بأمور ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Takathur describes three punishments for those who turn away: seeing Hell, seeing it with certainty, and being questioned about blessings.
rows.anchor: في سورة الهاكم بأن بين أن المعرضين عن دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Asr identifies the community’s three virtues as faith, good works, and exhorting one another to truth and patience.
rows.anchor: ثم شرف أمته في سورة والعصر بأمور ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Humaza describes three punishments for slanderers: wealth cannot save them, they are cast into the Crusher, and its doors are shut against escape.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أنه ينبذ في الحطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fil shows three ways God overturned the enemy’s plot: it failed, birds were sent against them, and they became eaten straw.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أرسل عليهم طير أبابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh was favored through ancestral harmony, provision from hunger, and security from fear.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أطعمهم من جوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma‘un depicts the deniers’ lowliness in orphan abuse and neglect of the poor, failure to honor the Creator through neglected or ostentatious prayer, and failure to benefit creatures by withholding small aid.
rows.anchor: وصف المكذبين بدينه بثلاثة أنواع من الصفات المذمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar crowns the prior chapters: its abundant gift encompasses their great merits, each greater than the world’s kingdom; Muhammad should worship in body and wealth and guide people through the next chapter.
rows.anchor: إنا أعطيناك هذه المناقب المتكاثرة المذكورة في السورة المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next command to disavow the world’s religions provokes greater hostility than attacks on life or wealth because people will sacrifice both to defend religion; for a universal messenger every person is like Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: عسف الناس على مذاهبهم وأديانهم أشد من عسفهم على أرواحهم وأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of abundant worldly and religious good assures protection and success, like God’s promise to guard the Messenger and His prior rescue of him.
rows.anchor: وعدا من الله إياه بالنصرة والحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the gift includes worldly and afterlife blessings not yet received in Mecca, God’s unfailing promise guarantees Muhammad will live, escape defeat, and grow stronger.
rows.anchor: والخلف في كلام الله تعالى محال ، فوجب في حكمة الله تعالى إبقاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh offered wealth, marriage, or leadership to win Muhammad over, God’s gift of this world and the next meant he should not be seduced by their concessions.
rows.anchor: إن كنت تفعل هذا طلبا للمال فنعطيك من المال ما تصير به أغنى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct divine address itself strengthens Muhammad’s heart more than a generic address, removing fear so he can undertake the difficult command to reject the world’s religions.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى تكلم معه لا بواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Muhammad obeyed, God fulfilled the promise with many followers entering Islam; discussion then turns inward, contrasting worldly seekers’ loss with the afterlife seeker whose soul reflects beings and knows God.
rows.anchor: إن أهل الدنيا يدخلون في دين الله أفواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an ends with the noblest path to knowledge: first God’s attributes in Al-Ikhlas, then creation’s ranks in Al-Falaq, then the human soul in Al-Nas.
rows.anchor: ثم ختم بذكر مراتب النفس الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural in إنا cannot mean multiple gods; it may mean angels and earlier prophets helped secure the gift, through Gabriel and Michael, Abraham’s prayer, Moses’ wish, and Jesus’ glad tidings.
rows.anchor: إلا إذا أريد أن هذه العطية مما سعى في تحصيلها الملائكة وجبريل وميكائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural magnifies the gift: the giver is Lord of heaven and earth, the recipient is Muhammad, and the gift itself is the exceedingly abundant Kawthar.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يكون ذلك محمولا على التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a small gift is honored by its great giver, like a king’s apple; Kawthar is already abundant and becomes still greater because it comes from the King of creation.
rows.anchor: الملك العظيم إذا رمى تفاحة لبعض عبيده على سبيل الإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hanafi rule permits a donor to reclaim a gift unless the recipient gives even a small compensation; pairing God’s gift with prayer and sacrifice signals compensation and ends any right of reclamation.
rows.anchor: من مذهب أبي حنيفة أنه يجوز للأجنبي أن يسترجع موهوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the subject before its report heightens confirmation: the hearer anticipates the great promise, and assurance from a great guarantor removes doubt about the immense gift.
rows.anchor: بنى الفعل على المبتدأ ، وذلك يفيد التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is more emphatic than simply saying that eyes do not become blind, and resembles a king saying, I will give, support, and attend to you.
rows.anchor: فإن الأبصار لا تعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening emphatic particle functions like an oath; truthful divine speech cannot be false, especially when intensified.
rows.anchor: صدر الجملة بحرف التأكيد الجاري محرى القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense promise means the gift was already established: past dignity is superior to future possibility, as the Prophetic saying declares he was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay.
rows.anchor: من كان في الزمان الماضي أبدا عزيزا مرعي الجانب مقضي الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s decisions to give happiness or distress, wealth or poverty, were settled eternally rather than newly arising.
rows.anchor: الإسعاد والإشفاء والإغناء والإفقار ، ليس أمرا يحدث الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared the causes of Muhammad’s felicity before his existence, so He would not neglect him after creation and worship.
rows.anchor: إنا قد هيأنا أسباب سعادتك قبل دخولك في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His election was pure grace rather than a reward for obedience, as shown by the report that acceptance and rejection occur without an underlying cause.
rows.anchor: إنما اخترناك بمجرد الفضل والإحسان منا إليك من غير موجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying We gave you rather than giving the messenger, prophet, scholar, or obedient person shows the gift was not caused by any quality but came from free divine choice.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو قال ذلك لأشعر أن تلك العطية وقعت معللة بذلك الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gift of guidance precedes human obedience: a created quality cannot affect the Creator; rather, eternal divine favor and approval lead the servant to obey.
rows.anchor: إعطاؤه للتوفيق والإرشاد سابق على طاعاتنا

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says he would not worship a Lord made pleased by obedience and angry by disobedience; divine approval and anger are eternal, while human actions are created and have no effect on them.
rows.anchor: لا أعبد ربا يرضيه طاعتي ويسخطه معصيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtaynaka suggests gratuitous giving more strongly than ataynaka, so Islam, Qur’an, prophethood, and lasting good name are pure favor rather than something earned or owed.
rows.anchor: الإيتاء يحتمل أن يكون واجبا وأن يكون تفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a generous giver does not stop once he begins and grace is not bounded by finite human merit, this wording promises continuing, increasing gifts.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أنه لا يبطلها ، بل كان كل يوم يزيد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Qur’an is also given, a gift implies ownership: Solomon’s gift was called God’s عطاؤنا; Muhammad cannot conceal Qur’an, while sharing knowledge is harmless and sharing a river is materially divisive.
rows.anchor: أن الإعطاء يوجب التمليك ، والملك سبب الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another linguistic distinction says iʿta is used for either little or much, while ita is used only for great things; thus Kawthar is a small gift relative to greater reserved ranks.
rows.anchor: الإعطاء يستعمل في القليل والكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Kawthar a gift can imply the promised stream is small compared with greater ranks, that water’s bliss previews other pleasures, that Paradise is bestowed more greatly, and that even abundant Kawthar is modest relative to Muhammad’s due.
rows.anchor: هذا الحوض كالشيء القليل الحقير بالنسبة إلى ما هو مدخر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may distinguish worldly Kawthar from religious Qur’an, or say all received goods are gifts while lasting remembrance and victory follow prayer and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أعطيناك لأنه دنيا ، والقرآن إيتاء لأنه دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar derives from abundance and means exceedingly abundant; Arabs used it for a large number, a generous giver, and thick rising dust, with al-Kumayt’s verse calling a man’s father Kawthar.
rows.anchor: الكوثر فهو في اللغة فوعل من الكثرة وهو المفرط في الكثرة

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt’s verse calls a man’s father Kawthar, illustrating the word for a person of abundant giving.
rows.anchor: وأنت كثير يا ابن مروان طيب وكان أبوك ابن الفضائل كوثرا

rows.speaker: السلف والخلف
rows.claim: The dominant transmitted interpretation is a river in Paradise; Anas reports the Prophet saw banks with hollow pearl domes and musk-scented water, and another Anas version describes milk-white, honey-sweet water and green birds; its drinkers attain God’s approval.
rows.anchor: أنه نهر في الجنة ، روى أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river may be called abundant because it has the most water and goodness, feeds other Paradise rivers, sends branches into every garden, has many drinkers, or holds many benefits; the Prophet called it a river of abundant good promised by God.
rows.anchor: إما إنه أكثر أنهار الجنة ماء وخيرا أو لأنه انفجر منه أنهار الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is the Basin; well-known reports support it, and it can be reconciled with the river if the river flows into the basin or springs from it.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أنه حوض والأخبار فيه مشهورة

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A third interpretation is the Prophet’s descendants, since the chapter answered critics who mocked him for having no sons; his family spread widely and produced major scholars and Imams, while the Umayyads left no notable surviving line.
rows.anchor: الكوثر أولاده قالوا : لأن هذه السورة إنما نزلت ردا على من عابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation is the abundant number of the Prophet’s scholars, like Israelite prophets: they share the law’s foundations but differ in subsidiary rulings as a mercy, preserve his remembrance, and may gather vast followings; even mistaken scholars are rewarded according to some.
rows.anchor: الكوثر علماء أمته وهو لعمري الخير الكثير لأنهم كأنبياء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth interpretation is prophethood, abundant good and the station next to Lordship; prophecy is a branch of knowledge of God, enables knowledge of other divine attributes, and Muhammad has the greatest share as universal, final, unsurpassed messenger.
rows.anchor: القول الخامس : الكوثر هو النبوة ، ولا شك أنها الخير الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s scripture is superior to earlier scriptures: Adam and Abraham received words, Moses scrolls, while Muhammad received the confirming, dominant Book; he challenges people with its composed form, whereas Adam was challenged over names.
rows.anchor: أما كتاب محمد عليه السلام ، فإنه هو الكتاب المهيمن على الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s ark was held on water, but Muhammad’s greater sign was a stone moving from its place, swimming to him, greeting him, and returning at his command when tested by Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl.
rows.anchor: لئن كنت صادقا فادع ذلك الحجر الذي هو في الجانب الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was honored when fire became cool and safe for him; Razi says Muhammad received a greater honor.
rows.anchor: وأكرم إبراهيم فجعل النار عليه بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad healed burned child Muhammad ibn Hatib by spitting on and wiping the wounds while praying for relief, after which he recovered completely.
rows.anchor: كنت طفلا فانصب القدر علي من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses split the sea on earth, while Muhammad split the moon in the sky and caused water to spring from his fingers; God shaded both with clouds.
rows.anchor: وأكرم موسى ففلق له البحر في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ white hand and staff-serpent are compared with Muhammad’s greater Qur’an and the serpents Abu Jahl saw; David’s singing mountains and softened iron are compared with stones praising Muhammad and his blessing a mangy sheep to give milk.
rows.anchor: وأكرم موسى باليد البيضاء ، وأكرم محمدا بإعظم من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David had mustered birds, while Muhammad rode the Buraq; Jesus raised the dead, while a poisoned sheep informed Muhammad, and he healed a woman’s leprosy and restored a man’s eye at Uhud.
rows.anchor: وأكرم داود بالطير المحشورة ومحمدا بالبراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet healed the leprosy of Muadh ibn Afra’s wife by touching her with a branch; after a man’s eye fell at Uhud, Muhammad restored it to its place.
rows.anchor: أن امرأة معاذ بن عفراء أتته وكانت برصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus knew what people hid at home; Muhammad learned what his uncle hid with Umm al-Fadl and informed him, leading al-Abbas to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: والرسول عرف ما أخفاه عمه مع أم الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God returned the sun for Muhammad when he awoke with his head in Ali’s lap, and again for Ali to pray Asr in its proper time.
rows.anchor: وفعل ذلك أيضا للرسول حين نام ورأسه في حجر علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon knew the language of birds, and Muhammad did too: he asked a man who had grieved a bird by taking its young to return the chick; the report of a wolf speaking to Muhammad is well known.
rows.anchor: أيكم فجع هذه بولدها ؟ فقال رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with Solomon’s month-long morning journey, Muhammad reached Jerusalem in an hour; his donkey Ya‘fur fetched people, an unmanageable she-camel submitted to him, and a lion yielded to Muadh when he identified himself as the Prophet’s envoy.
rows.anchor: وأكرم سليمان بمسيرة غدوة شهرا وأكرمه بالمسير إلى بيت المقدس في ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As jinn obeyed Solomon, creatures responded to Muhammad: a lizard confessed his prophethood, a gazelle returned after he held it as collateral, a palm trunk grieved his departure, and a snake in the cave said it longed to see him.
rows.anchor: وحين جاء الأعرابي بالضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad fed many people from little food and had too many miracles to count; the extraordinary messenger could rightly be called abundant good.
rows.anchor: ومعجزاته أكثر من أن تحصى وتعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth interpretation is the Qur’an, whose virtues are innumerable.
rows.anchor: القول السادس : الكوثر هو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh interpretation is Islam, abundant good for this world and the next; as knowledge or a path requiring knowledge it is wisdom, and Muhammad was its source for others.
rows.anchor: القول السابع : الكوثر الإسلام ، وهو لعمري الخير الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eighth interpretation is the great number of the Prophet’s followers; a report calls him Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ glad tidings, and an accepted intercessor, then describes every prophet hoping that a radiant, ablution-marked community is his.
rows.anchor: القول الثامن : الكوثر كثرة الأتباع والأشياع
